market.headline: Tech sold off hard into Nvidia's report: QQQ fell 2.7% to 661.75, below its 200-day average of 681.41, while SPY fell 1.9%. Tomorrow's main move is to buy nothing before Nvidia reports. Oracle is the first name to buy after the report.
market.day_type: An AI-led selloff ahead of Nvidia's report. Chip and AI-infrastructure stocks fell 4-8% as investors cut risk before the report and digested Nvidia's CEO turmoil, while Apple and Microsoft fell only about 1%. SPY traded 1.4x its normal volume, the 10-year yield is up to 5.1 from 4.9, and the Fed chair warned that AI can disappoint.
watch: NVDA earnings on Nov 17 (date estimated, time not confirmed). The result and Nvidia's answer on who runs the company will move every chip stock here.
QQQ 647.05, its 20-day low. A close below it means the tech selloff is widening; holding it means today was a pre-report flush.
SPY 729.58, its 200-day average. Above it, the long-term uptrend is intact; a close below it is the signal to cut risk.

stocks.headline: Fell 4.1% to 156.14 on 1.6x normal volume, the day before earnings. It is down 28.1% in 20 days. Morning call: right (148.8 held).
stocks.why: The selloff is about leadership and fear, not the business. Sales are up 106% and speeding up, the operating margin is 65%, and the stock trades at 10x next year's profit, its cheapest in 5 years. After the close, President Trump said he is fine with Jensen Huang returning as CEO, which takes some of the national-security fear off the table. Beats are already expected: Nvidia beat 8 quarters running and the stock still fell after 5 of them. Last time it gave no numeric outlook, so tomorrow the outlook and the CEO question matter more than the beat. A strong outlook lifts MU, AMD, TSM, ARM, AVGO, SMCI, CRWV and ORCL with it. A weak one pushes QQQ below 647.05.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view. The business is strong and cheap, but nobody knows who will lead it, and 4 analysts cut their targets last week.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A clear outlook and a settled CEO answer, with a close back above 170.0, move it to Add on dips. A guidance cut or a close below 148.8 moves it to Wait.
stocks.action: Don't buy before the report. If you own it, hold through the report and sell only on a close below 148.8.

levels.means: Above = the selloff is still a pullback in a strong business. Below = a new 52-week low, so get out and wait.
Above (today's high) = buyers are back after the report. Below = the pressure continues.
Above (Friday's high) = the post-report trend has turned, so start adding. Below = keep holding without adding.

stocks.headline: Fell 7.6% to 719.02, one of the day's worst. It is down 20.5% in 20 days and 42.7% below its 52-week high. Morning call: right.
stocks.why: Micron swings about twice as much as the market. Today's drop was fear about AI spending, not bad company news. The business is very strong: sales are up 345% and speeding up, the operating margin is 75%, the backlog is $134.0B, and cash of $38.4B is far more than its $2.8B of debt. At 4x next year's profit, a lot of bad news is already in the price. The real risk is a memory price cycle that turns. Nvidia's outlook tomorrow is the first test of that, before Micron reports on Dec 23.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view. It is cheap and growing fast, but memory stocks fall hardest when AI spending doubts spread, so don't add into the fall.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A strong Nvidia outlook with Micron back above 766.94 (its 200-day average) moves it to Add on dips.
stocks.action: Don't add before Nvidia reports. Add a small piece only if it closes back above 750.25 after the report.

levels.means: Above (Friday's low) = today's drop is repaired, so add a small piece. Below = sellers are still in control.
Above (200-day average) = the long-term uptrend is back. Below = treat rallies with caution.
Above (20-day low) = the range holds. Below = a deeper reset, so stand aside until it stabilizes.

stocks.headline: Fell 5.0% to 119.09 on half its normal volume. It is now 52.7% below its 52-week high. Morning call: too early.
stocks.why: The drop came on light volume, which points to sellers running out rather than big holders dumping the stock. Sales are up 30% and speeding up, and it has beaten forecasts 4 quarters running by wider margins each time. It has $664.0B of contracted backlog and $36.4B in cash. The stock trades at 11x next year's profit, cheaper than 93% of the last 5 years. The weak spot is next quarter: analysts expect profit per share to fall from a year ago because of building costs. The Dec 14 report usually moves the stock about 11%. If Nvidia disappoints, investors will doubt that Oracle's AI backlog turns into cash, and CRWV will fall with it.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view. A huge backlog, accelerating sales and a 5-year-low valuation outweigh one weaker quarter.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A close below 109.21 (its 52-week low) after Nvidia reports means the market doubts the backlog, so move to Wait.
stocks.action: Don't buy tomorrow before Nvidia reports. Buy a first third only on a close back above 121.76 after the report.
